raw_response:
I will still do it mostly the way I have done in recent years, then adjust a little by price and water. My land is only 3.5 mu, so every bag of fertilizer costs real money, but if I cut fertilizer too hard and lose yield, that hurts more. On my place, wheat and maize are the main income, so I will keep the better land in the wheat-maize rotation and leave 1 mu for cotton. For wheat, I will not save on base fertilizer because wheat here needs a strong stand before winter and enough strength when it greens up. I will use improved seed, put enough nitrogen first and then chase once in spring, and with my well I will water around three times if the year is normal. For maize after wheat, I will keep it simple and fast, because the stubble change is tight. I will use hybrid seed, give a good first fertilizer and one topdressing, and water about two times if rain is not enough. Cotton is slower and takes more watching, especially insects, so even on just 1 mu I will not let it go empty-handed. I will use improved seed, give enough bottom fertilizer, water more steadily, and spray more times than wheat or maize. I do watch what nearby farmers do, and if many of them cut fertilizer I still will not cut too much on wheat and maize, because wasting a little fertilizer is still better than losing a harvest.
